title: Nursing Home Abuse Linked to Corporate Profit Manipulation
discussion_signal: The post explicitly links NBER working paper w32258 and foregrounds its 68% estimate for profits tunneled through related-party real-estate and management payments. It translates the financial mechanism into a public accountability concern: apparent facility poverty, ownership opacity, possible reimbursement pressure, and the need to connect corporate structure with resident and worker protection. The post also distinguishes the operating facility from affiliated entities, making ownership transparency a central governance question.
linked_research_question: When related-party payments change the apparent profitability and liability of nursing homes, which ownership, reimbursement, staffing, and quality measures remain observable to residents, workers, and regulators?
limits: The post is an advocacy-oriented interpretation, not an independent replication of the NBER accounting analysis
The 68% estimate concerns tunneled profits and does not by itself establish illegal conduct or resident harm
A single LinkedIn post and its comments are not representative of nursing-home operators, residents, workers, or regulators
